title: What If a Cave Were Big Enough for Its Own Clouds? One Is

scenes.text: What if a cave were so big it made its own weather? One in Vietnam does.
A local man found the entrance in 1990, then couldn't find it again for eighteen years.
Explorers finally surveyed Son Doong in 2009: about nine kilometers long, with chambers 200 meters high.
That's 38 and a half million cubic meters. A Boeing 747 would fit inside its largest chamber.
Where the roof collapsed, sunlight pours in. A jungle grows inside, with trees over a hundred feet tall.
Heat from those openings evaporates the cave's river, and clouds form under the rock ceiling. Only about a thousand visitors a year get to see it.

description:
What if a cave were big enough to have its own weather? Hang Son Doong, in central Vietnam, is: at 38.5 million cubic meters it is the largest known cave on Earth.
A local man, Ho Khanh, found the entrance in 1990, could not find it again, and rediscovered it in 2008; a British-led team first went in the following year. The cave runs for about nine kilometers, with sections up to 200 meters high and 160 meters wide. Two collapsed sections of roof let in sunlight, so a forest with trees over 40 meters tall grows inside, and water evaporating from the river forms clouds beneath the ceiling. About 1,000 visitors are allowed in each year.
